item.title: Fix bug in window.py so python3 -m unittest passes
item.brief: Repository: fix-off-by-one. Running `python3 -m unittest` in the repository currently fails. Find the bug in `window.py` and fix it so every test passes. Do not modify any test file. The function must be correct for every valid input, not only the inputs the tests cover: check boundary cases (empty input, single element, first and last index, off-by-one at the window edges, and any input length or size where the window or slice logic could go wrong) and reason through them explicitly. Keep the fix minimal and readable, with no unnecessary comments. Verify by running `python3 -m unittest` and report the full output. Commit the fix on the local branch with a clear commit message. Do not push anything.

pr.body:
Approach: the comprehension ranged over range(len(items) - size), which omits the window starting at len(items) - size. Changed to range(len(items) - size + 1). Key file: window.py (one line).

Checks: before, python3 -m unittest fails 2 of 3 tests. After, it passes all 3 tests. Boundary cases verified: [] size 1 -> []; [1] size 1 -> [[1]]; [1,2] size 3 -> []; [1,2] size 2 -> [[1,2]]; [1,2,3] size 1 -> three singletons; [1,2,3] size 3 -> one window; [1,2,3,4] size 2 -> three windows.

Assumptions: size <= 0 still raises ValueError, unchanged. No test file was modified.
pr.summary: Made sliding_windows return the final window. Before: the last window was dropped (2 of 3 tests failing). Now: all windows, including the whole list when size equals len, are returned.
pr.title: Fix off-by-one that dropped the last sliding window

risk.why: One-line range bound fix in window.py with no API change. Covered by the existing unit tests and explicit boundary checks. Reviewer confirmed low risk.
